lead: Digital selective calling lets one radio ring another, the way a phone does. You talk by voice afterwards; DSC only makes the call. In distress the same system sends who you are and where you are in a single burst of data.

sections.title: A data call on 70, then voice

qa.q: Will my DSC radio hear a distress alert while I'm talking on another channel?
qa.a: Yes: a fixed **DSC** set has a second receiver that listens on channel 70 all the time, whatever voice channel you are using and whether or not dual watch is on.

blocks.p: A **DSC** call is a short digital message on **channel 70**, which carries data only, never voice. It names the station called, the station calling, the priority and the channel for the conversation. A fixed DSC set has a second receiver that listens on 70 all the time, whatever voice channel you are using and whether or not dual watch is on.

fig.note: Chatting on 72, the set still hears an alert on 70

qa.q: Can I put my own MMSI number into a charter yacht's radio?
qa.a: No: the **MMSI** is issued to the vessel with her ship radio licence, not to a person. It is programmed into the set once and stays with the yacht.

blocks.p: The **MMSI** is the number DSC calls. It always has **nine figures**. A ship's MMSI begins with the three-figure **MID**, the code of her flag state, so a rescue centre sees at once where she is registered. A coast station's number begins with 00, a group's with a single 0.

fig.title: Reading an MMSI
lines: 238 = MID: the flag state, here Croatia

blocks.cap: Example numbers: the zeros in front tell you what kind of station it is.

blocks.p: The MMSI is issued to the **vessel** with her ship radio licence, not to a person. It is programmed into the set once and stays with the yacht: a guest cannot put in his own. A set with no MMSI can send neither a call nor an alert, so on a charter yacht have the base put it right before you sail.

sections.title: Ringing one yacht, or your flotilla

qa.q: How do I test the DSC on my VHF without sending a false alert?
qa.a: Send a routine **individual call** to a friend's MMSI and see that it arrives. Never test DSC with the red DISTRESS button.

list: Choose **individual call**, enter or pick her MMSI and propose an intership channel such as 72.
Send. Her set rings and shows who is calling.
She acknowledges, both sets go to the proposed channel, and you talk by voice.
A **group call** rings every set that holds the group MMSI and sends them all to the channel named: go there and listen for the lead boat.

blocks.p: An **all-ships** call sounds an alarm on every set in range. It is kept for distress, urgency and safety, never used to ask the fleet for a spare part. To **test** DSC, send a routine individual call to a friend's MMSI and see that it arrives. Never test with the red button.

qa.q: How do I send a DSC distress alert with the red button?
qa.a: Lift the cover, press and hold the **DISTRESS** button for about five seconds until the set confirms the alert has gone. The set switches to 16: send your voice MAYDAY there and keep listening.

blocks.p: The DISTRESS button sits under a cover so that it cannot be pressed by accident. **Lift the cover, press and hold for about five seconds** until the set confirms the alert has gone.

head: The alert carries
From
rows: The GPS feed, or entered by hand

blocks.p: With a minute in hand, pick the **nature of distress** first: fire, flooding, collision, grounding, sinking, man overboard. Rescuers then know what to bring. With no time, the button alone sends an undesignated distress. The set repeats the alert by itself about every four minutes until a station acknowledges it. It also switches to 16: send your voice MAYDAY there and keep listening.

qa.q: What does NO POSITION on my DSC radio display mean?
qa.a: No GPS data reaches the set, so an alert would say who you are but not **where**. Switch the GPS or plotter on, or enter position and time by hand and update it regularly.

blocks.p: An alert is only as good as the data behind it. Without a GPS feed and with no position entered, it says who you are but not **where**. Read the DSC display before you leave the berth.

sections.title: When the alarm sounds on your set

qa.q: What should I do if my VHF sends a false DSC distress alert?
qa.a: Do not just switch the set off: **cancel the alert** on it if it has that function, then tell all stations by voice on 16, with your name, MMSI, position and the time it was sent.

blocks.p: Your set sounds an alarm and shows a distress alert: an MMSI, a position, a nature of distress. Silence the alarm, **write the details down** and listen on 16 for the voice MAYDAY. Do not acknowledge by DSC: that is normally left to the coast station, whose acknowledgement stops the casualty's set repeating.
If your own set sends an alert by mistake, do not just switch it off: a search may already be starting. Cancel the alert on the set if it has that function, then tell everyone by voice on 16.

fig.title: Cancelling a false alert, on 16
lines: ALL STATIONS, ALL STATIONS, ALL STATIONS
CANCEL MY DISTRESS ALERT OF 0915 UTC

blocks.rule: A false alert is nothing to hide. Cancel it at once, with your name, MMSI, position and the time it was sent.
